when_to_use: dusty loop-based jazzhop where familiar material reveals a new shade on each return, 75-95 BPM, Rhodes and grounded bass with late-arriving lead

defaults.feel: swung-16th, deep pocket, dusty and relaxed

signature_moves: begin with a reassuring 2-4 chord loop, then let one repeat reveal doubt through a small reharm; preserve the bass foundation while changing the upper color
borrowed color: Dm9 -> Bbmaj7 -> Ebmaj7#11 (bII color) -> A7alt, used as a brief window into a colder room before the loop returns
gospel passing: Gm11 -> G#dim7 -> Am9, allowing one upward step to feel like a small recovery
chromatic bass walkup under a held upper voicing, creating forward motion without making the loop leave its emotional center
cadence_options: secondary ii-V into Gm11: Am7 -> D9 -> Gm11 when the loop needs a gentle hinge rather than a final cadence
plagal settle: Gm11 -> Dm9 with no dominant when the return should feel familiar and unforced
deceptive: A7alt -> Bbmaj7 instead of Dm when comfort should be delayed for one more pass
avoid: chord density as a substitute for pocket; identity comes from groove, texture, silence, and the meaning of each return (see style-cheatsheets Lofi jazz)
the exact same voicing looped with zero reharm, response, subtraction, or register change for the whole tune (see ../references/cliche-register.md)

hook_archetypes.name: half-remembered-fragment
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a brief 2-bar thought that lands on the '&' of 2, then stops as though it has forgotten the rest of the sentence
hook_archetypes.contour: fall by a 3rd; on a later repeat, answer from another octave so the memory feels familiar but more distant
hook_archetypes.first_appears: over the first bare loop, before the arrangement feels complete

hook_archetypes.name: color-that-changes
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a sustained top color is re-struck only when the reharm arrives, making the harmonic change feel discovered rather than announced
hook_archetypes.contour: hold the 9th or #11 so the harmony underneath changes its emotional meaning while the melodic identity stays still
hook_archetypes.first_appears: the second loop, after the listener has learned the original harmony

settle.note_lengths: the lead is reluctant to speak: use sparse fragments, long rests, and only enough notes to make the silence feel intentional
settle.contour: circle close to the tonic and one fragile color tone, avoiding a complete melodic statement
settle.placement: deep in the pocket, as though the phrase arrives after listening to the loop

develop.note_lengths: each loop remembers one additional detail; add only one meaningful phrase, extension, or answer at a time
develop.contour: reach slightly higher and let the reharm color enter the melody without turning it into a dramatic climax
develop.placement: in the pocket, with slightly clearer intention than the settle phase

lift.note_lengths: this is the most exposed point, not necessarily the busiest; allow one phrase to last longer than expected
lift.contour: hold the highest color tone across the reharm so the harmony changes its meaning underneath
lift.placement: a touch more forward while remaining restrained

dissolve.note_lengths: phrases lose pieces of themselves until only a trace remains
dissolve.contour: return toward the tonic or the loop's safest tone, but avoid making the ending feel fully explained
dissolve.placement: loosen and drift, as though the loop continues after the listener leaves

drum_skeleton.low_energy: the drummer protects the empty space: dusty kick on 1 and the 'a' of 2, laid-back snare on 2 and 4, sparse hat
drum_skeleton.mid_energy: add subtle swung-16th hat ghosts and one syncopated kick echo that answers the bass phrase rather than merely thickening the bar
drum_skeleton.high_energy: remain restrained; open one hat accent and place a short fill at the loop boundary, then immediately return to the pocket

arrangement_defaults.layout_rules: let the listener enter while the Rhodes loop is already breathing. Bass makes the room feel grounded; drums arrive as quiet confirmation; lead appears only after the pocket feels trustworthy. Reuse the same loop across contrasting arrangement states, developing through subtraction, addition, selective reharm, and foreground exchange. Strip to keys and bass when the music needs to feel most exposed. The lead should disappear often enough that its return feels remembered rather than scheduled.

anti_boredom_rules: each loop repeat must reveal or conceal one detail through subtraction, addition, reharm, articulation, register, or instrumentation; changes must feel motivated rather than decorative
the reharm must occur at least once beneath a sustained color so a familiar idea acquires a different emotional meaning
no 2-bar loop may repeat more than 4 times without a perceptible textural, harmonic, melodic, or arrangement change
do not let every voice behave with the same intensity; foreground and background must exchange roles across the form
protect the empty space around the motif; silence is part of the hook, not unused capacity
the final return must omit or alter one element the listener has learned to expect

bass_behavior.role: fat low-end anchor under a short loop
bass_behavior.rhythmic_relationship: echoes selected kick syncopations without continuous doubling
bass_behavior.density: sparse and repetitive with occasional chromatic walkups
bass_behavior.articulation: rounded sustain, shortened before crowded kick moments

groove_intent.feel: dusty swung-sixteenth pocket with deliberate space
groove_intent.kick: soft anchors and one syncopated echo
groove_intent.ensemble_relationship: texture changes around a stable pocket rather than increasing rhythmic density

distinguishing_traits: single short loop developed through subtraction and addition
texture and filtering are primary form devices
lead enters late and remains secondary to pocket
